To: Shared/Ops & HR
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: DRAFT — Brian’s brief for Embakasi, Monday 30 November

DRAFT — for my review tonight, not for circulation to the casuals.

Brian,

Thank you for taking this on. After six years working together, I know I don’t need to tell you how to talk to people. What you need from me is a straight account, clear limits on what we can promise, and a plan that doesn’t depend on everyone being paid before the Kisumu trucks leave.

The short version: Friday’s payment file failed. Nobody in that file was paid. M-Pesa is approved as the replacement, with an extra KES 500 for every affected casual and the charges covered by us. Kevin’s current realistic estimate is Monday by 11am, not before loading. That is an estimate, not a confirmed payment time. The trucks need to leave at 9am, so we must deal honestly with that gap.

What happened on Friday

The bank rejected the bulk file at 1:52pm on Friday 27 November. It contained 212 payments. The beneficiary-reference field was too long for the bank’s new template following its platform upgrade on 25 November. The bank confirmed that none of the payments in that file had been processed.

The rejection alert went to the old Finance mailbox. Kevin only saw it after 5pm, after the bank cut-off. We failed to catch and correct it in time. This was not caused by the casuals, and it is not something they should have to defend themselves over.

Njeri has approved paying through M-Pesa instead. Peninah has confirmed 198 phone numbers; 14 people were unreachable, mostly from the new Athi River intake. Being unreachable is not the same as having supplied a wrong number. Those cases still need checking face to face.

What you can say and commit to

You can confirm:
- All 212 people on the affected list are due their outstanding Friday pay.
- M-Pesa is the approved payment route.
- Every casual on that list has an approved additional KES 500 for Monday lunch and fare, to be paid in the same M-Pesa batch.
- The company is covering the M-Pesa charges; they will not be deducted from anyone’s pay.
- Peninah will be at Embakasi from 7:30am with the list to check the 14 outstanding numbers and deal with individual queries. She will have her laptop for anyone who wants a printed payslip.
- Management accepts responsibility and is apologising in person.

Kevin’s estimate is money on phones by 11am Monday. If you give that estimate, give the qualification in the same breath: it is the current expected time, not a guarantee. Approval is not proof that the batch has been sent, and a batch being sent is not proof that every individual has received it.

Please do not promise payment by 9am, “by lunch”, or before someone starts loading. Mombasa in 2024 is exactly what we must not repeat: the supervisor said “by lunch”, the money arrived at 4pm, and half the shift sat down. No time we cannot keep.

Do not describe the KES 500 as cash available at the depot or as something people get only if they load. It is approved for every casual on the affected list. Do not promise further compensation, an alternative cash payout or an immediate fix for every individual payment problem without approval and confirmation.

Before the morning meeting

You’re arriving at 5:30am. Please get Joseph’s overnight update and speak to Ouma privately before addressing everyone. Ask Joseph to help arrange that without making it look like Ouma is being summoned for discipline.

Ouma is loud, but he is not a bad man. He has four children and rent to meet. Listen first. Something along these lines:

“Ouma, I wanted you to hear this from me before we speak to everyone. Friday’s pay failed on our side. You and the others did nothing wrong. I know people have rent and families depending on this money. I’ll explain exactly what is approved and what is still an estimate. Tell me what the main concerns are.”

Do not ask him to guarantee that everyone will load or treat him as responsible for everyone else’s behaviour. Ask for his help keeping the conversation calm, without making that a condition of dealing with his pay.

Please check with Kevin before the group briefing: is the M-Pesa arrangement ready, does the 11am estimate still stand, and how are the 198 confirmed numbers and 14 outstanding checks being handled? Don’t assume the confirmed payments must wait for all 14; equally, don’t announce separate batches unless Kevin confirms that arrangement.

I’m awake from 4:30am. WhatsApp me before I board if anything changes: the payment estimate, the mood, a refusal to load, or any risk to the 9am departure. My flight is at 7:05am. We should settle the HR contact for the period I’m in the air before I board, rather than leave you relying on an unanswered call.

What to say to the group

Use your own words, but this is the substance:

“Morning, everyone. I owe you an apology on behalf of management. Your Friday pay did not go through. The bank rejected our payment file, and we did not pick up the rejection in time to correct it before the cut-off. That is our mistake, not yours.

“We have approval to pay through M-Pesa, including an extra KES 500 each for Monday lunch and fare for everyone on the affected list. The company is covering the M-Pesa charges.

“Finance’s current estimate is payment by 11am today. I need to be honest: that is an estimate, not a guaranteed time, and I cannot promise money before loading or before the trucks leave at 9.

“Peninah will be here from 7:30 with the list. Fourteen people still need their numbers checked with her directly. If you have a question about your own pay or need a payslip, please see her privately.

“I know another promise is not the same as money received. I will give you the next update at 8am, even if the update is that we are still waiting for confirmation.”

Keep that 8am update commitment. A reliable update is something we can control; the exact arrival time is not. Don’t read out people’s numbers or individual pay details to the group.

If Ouma’s group refuses to load

Do not turn it into a public contest with Ouma. Acknowledge the refusal, establish who is affected and whether any loading can continue safely, and bring HR into the response immediately. Our procedure requires Operations and HR to handle stoppages together. Joseph should not be left to deal with it alone, and neither should you.

You can say:

“I hear that you are not willing to load until payment arrives. I am asking you to continue loading so we can meet the Kisumu departure, but I will not pretend the payment is confirmed before then. We need to work through this with HR now.”

The procedure says stoppages are not a grievance channel. That is not a reason to refuse to hear the grievance. The normal route is through the shift supervisor, then HR within 48 hours; Monday’s stoppage needs joint Ops/HR handling there and then.

No dismissal, threats of dismissal, or threats about contracts on Monday. No “load or don’t come back”, and no suggestion that pay or the approved KES 500 depends on cooperation. Keep a factual record of concerns, discussions, decisions and operational impact, not a list of supposed troublemakers.

The 9am departure

Do not wait until the estimated 11am payment to decide what happens to the trucks. At the 8am update, assess actual loading progress with Joseph. If a 9am departure is doubtful, escalate immediately to Njeri and the relevant transport/customer contact so they can pursue a revised offloading slot or other authorised operational arrangements. Do not promise the mill will hold the slot.

Keep safe loading moving where people are willing, without intimidation or shortcuts. Don’t put untrained people onto loading work just to save the departure. If the slot cannot be met, report it plainly and get an authorised decision rather than making a payment promise to force the trucks out.

After payment starts

Have Kevin confirm the batch status and Peninah help follow up individual non-receipts or discrepancies. Don’t announce “everyone has been paid” on the strength of the first few confirmations. Keep the unresolved cases open until checked.

The tone throughout is simple: we caused this, we are sorry, and we will give people facts rather than another moving deadline. You don’t need to go in defensive. They have every reason to be upset.

Achieng
